_comment: Pages and responses the Paradox panel gives to the bridge, and what src/api/status.js and src/api/alarm.js make of them. "page" / "response.body" is an inline string or {"file": "<path relative to tests/>"}. A get_status "expected" is the whole result of getStatus(): statuszone and useraccess as the panel writes them, alarms (the areas in alarm) and troubles (the active troubles) as 0-based indexes into tbl_areanam and tbl_troublename of the index page; a page that does not contain the name tbl_alarmes or tbl_troubles at all reads that list as empty, and one that contains the name without a table in the expected format fails like the other tables. "error" is the exact message of the failure; messages other than the parse error and the bridge's own "... answered with the login page" come from the JavaScript HTTP client (axios 0.18) and only the fact of failing is portable. body_ignoring_responses apply alike to arm, disarm and sendKeepAlive; login_page_responses are per operation: a command or keep-alive answered with the login page (what the fake panel serves without a session, see README.md) fails. Rows with a known_bug (catalog in README.md) are in known_bugs/status_pages.json, in the same groups.

get_status.note: tbl_alarmes = new Array(): no area in alarm. tbl_troubles = new Array("16","19","38"): on the captured index page, Bell output disconnected, time and date lost, tamper on the PCS module.
